---
title: "02b Movement thresholds"
output: html_notebook
editor_options:
  chunk_output_type: console
---

Derives the 59, 99 and 512 m movement thresholds used throughout the
pipeline. Extracts every British-species row from the European butterfly
movement-distance compilation (Phaidra, univie.ac.at) that qualifies as a
mean movement distance (MDD), collapses these to one value per species,
and cross-references them with the urban-associated species list from the
author's thesis. The species tables are written to
`data/movement_distances/`. The thresholds themselves are set in
`03_National_ECS.Rmd` (`fixed_thresholds`).

```{r setup}
source(here::here("scripts", "00_setup.R"))
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)

path <- file.path(raw_data_dir, "European_butterflies_movement_distances.xlsx")
```

# Load the workbook

Reads the three sheets of the workbook: the species codes, the movement distances and the sources.

```{r load_sheets}
species_codes <- read_excel(path, sheet = "Species codes")
movement      <- read_excel(path, sheet = "Movement distances")
sources       <- read_excel(path, sheet = "Sources")

cat("Movement-distance rows (all species):", nrow(movement), "\n")
cat("Species in the code list:", nrow(species_codes), "\n")
cat("Sources cited:", nrow(sources), "\n")
```

# Define the British species list

Standard British resident/breeding butterfly species; excludes rare
migrants and long-extinct species not part of the current fauna.

```{r british_species_list}
british_species <- c(
  "Aglais io", "Aglais urticae", "Anthocharis cardamines", "Aphantopus hyperantus",
  "Argynnis adippe", "Argynnis aglaja", "Aricia agestis", "Aricia artaxerxes",
  "Boloria euphrosyne", "Boloria selene", "Callophrys rubi", "Celastrina argiolus",
  "Coenonympha pamphilus", "Coenonympha tullia", "Cupido minimus",
  "Erebia aethiops", "Erebia epiphron", "Erynnis tages", "Euphydryas aurinia",
  "Gonepteryx rhamni", "Hamearis lucina", "Hesperia comma", "Hipparchia semele",
  "Lasiommata megera", "Leptidea sinapis", "Lycaena phlaeas",
  "Lysandra bellargus", "Lysandra coridon", "Maniola jurtina",
  "Melitaea athalia", "Melitaea cinxia", "Melanargia galathea",
  "Nymphalis c-album", "Ochlodes sylvanus", "Pararge aegeria",
  "Phengaris arion", "Pieris brassicae", "Pieris napi", "Pieris rapae",
  "Plebejus argus", "Polyommatus icarus", "Pyrgus malvae", "Pyronia tithonus",
  "Satyrium pruni", "Thymelicus acteon", "Thymelicus lineola",
  "Thymelicus sylvestris", "Vanessa atalanta"
)

british_codes <- species_codes |> filter(Species %in% british_species)
cat("British species matched in this workbook's code list:", nrow(british_codes), "of", length(british_species), "\n")
```

# Join and clean

Keeps the movement-distance rows for British species and attaches each row's source details.

```{r join_and_clean}
data <- movement |>
  inner_join(british_codes, by = "SpeciesCode") |>
  left_join(sources, by = c("SourceID" = "Source ID")) |>
  # MovementDistance is stored as text in the source file. A handful of
  # rows hold inequality-bounded values such as "<500" or ">1000", which
  # cannot be a single mean and become NA here.
  mutate(MovementDistance = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(MovementDistance)))

cat("British-species movement-distance rows:", nrow(data), "\n")
```

# Filter to a mean movement distance metric

Keeps only rows directly comparable to Sekar (2012)'s mean dispersal
distance:

- `DistanceType == "Distance between successive captures"`, the standard
  mark-recapture movement-distance metric. This excludes "sum of
  distances between points of capture" (cumulative track length, not a
  movement distance), "distance between first and last capture" (net
  displacement, sensitive to how long the study ran), "length of flight
  path" (within-territory patrol tracking) and "colonisation distance" (a
  rare long-range event on a different scale, km rather than m).
- `TypeOfValue == "mean"`, not median, maximum, SD, SE or an individual
  example.
- `CompleteDataset == "Yes"`, the study's full dataset rather than a
  filtered subset.

Every qualifying row is kept individually (sex-specific and combined)
rather than pre-aggregated to one number per species, so each source and
sample size stays visible and any aggregation decision can be made by
inspection.

```{r filter_qualifying}
qualifying <- data |>
  filter(
    DistanceType == "Distance between successive captures",
    TypeOfValue == "mean",
    CompleteDataset == "Yes",
    !is.na(MovementDistance)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(Species, MovementDistance, Sex, nMoveTotal, SourceID, Reference) |>
  arrange(Species, MovementDistance)

cat("Qualifying rows:", nrow(qualifying), "\n")
cat("British species with at least one qualifying row:", length(unique(qualifying$Species)), "of", length(british_species), "\n")
```

# Results

```{r print_results}
print(as.data.frame(qualifying), row.names = FALSE)
```

Writes the qualifying rows to a CSV in `data/movement_distances/`.

```{r write_csv}
out_path <- here::here("data", "movement_distances", "british_species_movement_distances.csv")
write.csv(qualifying, out_path, row.names = FALSE)
cat("Written to:", out_path, "\n")
```

# One value per species

Collapses `qualifying` to one figure per species. Rows for both sexes
(`Sex == "B"`) are preferred where a source reports them, as the pooled
population-level estimate that a single MDD per species represents. If no
source reported a combined value, male and female rows are averaged; if
neither exists, sex-unspecified rows (`Sex` is `NA`) are used. The
workbook's own column description says an unspecified sex "in most of
these cases... likely pertains to both sexes", so these rows are treated
as equivalent to "B" rather than dropped.

`%in%` is used for the sex checks rather than `==`, because `==` against
a column containing `NA` returns `NA` rather than `FALSE` (`NA == "B"` is
`NA`), which breaks `any()` and `case_when()` logic downstream.

```{r one_value_per_species}
# The source workbook stores "sex not reported" as the literal text "NA",
# not a true missing value (is.na(Sex) is FALSE for these rows, while
# Sex == "NA" is TRUE). is.na() alone misses them, so both are checked.
is_unspecified_sex <- function(x) is.na(x) | x == "NA"

per_species <- qualifying |>
  group_by(Species) |>
  summarise(
    n_rows      = n(),
    value_both  = mean(MovementDistance[Sex %in% "B"]),
    value_mf    = mean(MovementDistance[Sex %in% c("M", "F")]),
    value_nasex = mean(MovementDistance[is_unspecified_sex(Sex)]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    MDD = case_when(
      !is.nan(value_both)  ~ value_both,
      !is.nan(value_mf)    ~ value_mf,
      !is.nan(value_nasex) ~ value_nasex
    ),
    basis = case_when(
      !is.nan(value_both)  ~ "both sexes",
      !is.nan(value_mf)    ~ "M/F averaged",
      !is.nan(value_nasex) ~ "sex unspecified"
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(Species, MDD, basis, n_rows) |>
  arrange(MDD)

cat("Species with a usable value:", nrow(per_species), "of", length(british_species), "\n\n")
print(as.data.frame(per_species |> mutate(MDD = round(MDD, 1))), row.names = FALSE)

out_path2 <- here::here("data", "movement_distances", "british_species_mdd_one_per_species.csv")
write.csv(per_species, out_path2, row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nWritten to:", out_path2, "\n")
```

# Species with no qualifying row

These species need a different metric, or are not in the compilation for
this `DistanceType`.

```{r missing_species}
print(setdiff(british_species, unique(qualifying$Species)))
```

# Cross-reference against the thesis's urban-associated species list

Table 2.4 of the thesis (Neal, 2025) lists the urban-associated species
the study is built around, each with its habitat specialism as classified
there. This checks which of them have a usable MDD in `per_species`
above.

```{r thesis_species_list}
thesis_species <- tribble(
  ~Species,                    ~CommonName,                ~Family,        ~RedListStatus,  ~HabitatSpecialist,
  "Aglais io",                  "Peacock",                  "Nymphalidae",  "Least concern",  "No",
  "Aglais urticae",             "Small Tortoiseshell",      "Nymphalidae",  "Least concern",  "No",
  "Anthocharis cardamines",     "Orange-tip",                "Pieridae",     "Least concern",  "No",
  "Apatura iris",                "Purple Emperor",           "Nymphalidae",  "Least concern",  "Woodland",
  "Aphantopus hyperantus",      "Ringlet",                   "Nymphalidae",  "Least concern",  "No",
  "Argynnis paphia",             "Silver-Washed Fritillary",  "Nymphalidae",  "Least concern",  "Woodland",
  "Aricia agestis",              "Brown Argus",               "Lycaenidae",   "Least concern",  "No",
  "Celastrina argiolus",         "Holly Blue",                "Lycaenidae",   "Least concern",  "No",
  "Colias crocea",               "Clouded Yellow",            "Pieridae",     "Least concern",  "No",
  "Cupido minimus",              "Small Blue",                "Lycaenidae",   "Near Threatened","Chalk grassland",
  "Favonius quercus",            "Purple Hairstreak",         "Lycaenidae",   "Least concern",  "No",
  "Gonepteryx rhamni",           "Brimstone",                 "Pieridae",     "Least concern",  "No",
  "Lasiommata megera",           "Wall Brown",                 "Nymphalidae",  "Endangered",     "No",
  "Limenitis camilla",           "White Admiral",              "Nymphalidae",  "Vulnerable",     "Woodland",
  "Lycaena phlaeas",             "Small Copper",               "Lycaenidae",   "Least concern",  "No",
  "Maniola jurtina",             "Meadow Brown",               "Nymphalidae",  "Least concern",  "No",
  "Melanargia galathea",         "Marbled White",              "Nymphalidae",  "Least concern",  "No",
  "Ochlodes sylvanus",           "Large Skipper",              "Hesperiidae",  "Least concern",  "No",
  "Pararge aegeria",             "Speckled Wood",              "Nymphalidae",  "Least concern",  "No",
  "Pieris brassicae",            "Large White",                "Pieridae",     "Least concern",  "No",
  "Pieris napi",                 "Green-veined White",         "Pieridae",     "Least concern",  "No",
  "Pieris rapae",                "Small White",                "Pieridae",     "Least concern",  "No",
  "Polygonia c-album",           "Comma",                      "Nymphalidae",  "Least concern",  "No",
  "Polyommatus icarus",          "Common Blue",                "Lycaenidae",   "Least concern",  "No",
  "Pyronia tithonus",            "Gatekeeper",                 "Nymphalidae",  "Least concern",  "No",
  "Satyrium w-album",            "White-letter Hairstreak",    "Lycaenidae",   "Vulnerable",     "No",
  "Thymelicus lineola",          "Essex Skipper",              "Hesperiidae",  "Least concern",  "No",
  "Thymelicus sylvestris",       "Small Skipper",              "Hesperiidae",  "Least concern",  "No",
  "Vanessa atalanta",            "Red Admiral",                "Nymphalidae",  "Least concern",  "No",
  "Vanessa cardui",              "Painted Lady",                "Nymphalidae",  "Least concern",  "No"
)

cat("Thesis urban-associated species list: n =", nrow(thesis_species), "\n")
```

Two species with a qualifying MDD are excluded here, although
`HabitatSpecialist` in the thesis table does not flag both of them:
*Cupido minimus* is flagged there as a chalk grassland specialist, but
*Aricia agestis* is marked "No" despite also being a grassland species
in practice. Neither is a plausible match for a woodland connectivity
threshold, so both are excluded manually rather than by filtering on
`HabitatSpecialist` alone.

```{r thesis_comparison}
non_woodland_exclusions <- c("Cupido minimus", "Aricia agestis")

thesis_matched <- thesis_species |>
  inner_join(per_species, by = "Species") |>
  filter(!Species %in% non_woodland_exclusions) |>
  arrange(MDD)

cat("Thesis species with a usable MDD:", nrow(thesis_matched) + length(non_woodland_exclusions),
    "of", nrow(thesis_species), "\n")
cat("After excluding non-woodland specialists:", nrow(thesis_matched), "\n\n")

print(as.data.frame(thesis_matched |> mutate(MDD = round(MDD, 1))), row.names = FALSE)

out_path3 <- here::here("data", "movement_distances", "thesis_species_mdd_matched.csv")
write.csv(thesis_matched, out_path3, row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nWritten to:", out_path3, "\n")

cat("\nThesis species with no usable MDD under this filter:\n")
print(setdiff(thesis_species$Species, per_species$Species) |> sort())
```
